title: Coherent biduality over a complete Noetherian local ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal. Assume that $R$ is complete, meaning the canonical homomorphism $R\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R/\mathfrak m^n$ is an isomorphism. Work in the ordinary module derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with $R\operatorname{Hom}$ the internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. Let $D_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$ denote the full subcategory of objects whose cohomology modules are finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] in every degree, without any boundedness requirement. Superscripts $+$, $-$ and $b$ mean, respectively, cohomology bounded below, bounded above and bounded on both sides. There exists $\Omega\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$ for which $\mathbb D(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,\Omega)$ is an anti-equivalence $D_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)\to D_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$, exchanges $D^+_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$ and $D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$, and preserves $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$. For every $K\in D_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$, the canonical biduality map $K\to R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,\Omega),\Omega)$ adjoint to evaluation is an isomorphism, naturally in $K$.

source.place: Tag 0BFR, lemma-ubiquity-dualizing, case (2), combined with Tag 0A7C, lemma-dualizing (including unbounded coherent complexes and canonical biduality). This packages the existence and the duality property, not a conservativity assertion for an arbitrary semidualizing complex.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-power-series-presentation] to $R$, whose maximal-ideal-adic completeness is exactly the hypothesis. It supplies a surjective local homomorphism $q:A\to R$ from a complete Noetherian regular local ring $A$. Only regularity and surjectivity of this presentation are needed below; no assertion about formal fibres or excellence is used. By [lem-trf-regular-local-bounded-injective-resolution], $A[0]$ has a bounded injective representative.

source.place: Tag 0BFR, lemma-ubiquity-dualizing, proof of case (2): Cohen presentation and regular-local input.

proof.text: The only cohomology of $A[0]$ is the cyclic $A$-module $A$ in degree zero. The scalar-action map $A[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A[0],A[0])$ is an isomorphism: compute into a bounded injective representative $I$ of $A[0]$, which is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]; evaluation at $1$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_A(A[0],I)$ with $I$, and scalar action becomes the identity of $A[0]$ under this identification. The quotient $R$ is a finite $A$-module generated by $1$. Apply [lem-trf-finite-map-dualizing-transfer] to $q$ and $L=A[0]$. Thus $\Omega=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(R,A[0])$ has finite $R$-cohomology, a bounded injective $R$-representative $J$, and the scalar-action isomorphism $h:R[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(\Omega,\Omega)$. In particular $\Omega\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$.

source.place: Tag 0AX0, lemma-dualizing-finite, applied in Tag 0BFR case (2); explicit verification of its hypotheses on A[0].

proof.text: Fix $K\in D_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$. By [lem-trf-coherent-rhom-finite-injective-dimension], applied with $L=\Omega$ and its bounded injective representative, $\mathbb D(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,\Omega)$ again has finite cohomology in every degree. Therefore the contravariant derived Hom functor restricts to $D_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$.

source.place: Tag 0A7C, lemma-dualizing, first paragraph; Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-homothety-evaluation-biduality] with $L=\Omega$. Step 2 supplies a bounded injective representative and scalar-action isomorphism; $R$ is Noetherian. Thus, for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$, the canonical evaluation-transpose map $\delta_K:K\to\mathbb D\mathbb D(K)$ is an isomorphism, naturally in $K$.

source.place: Tag 0A7C, lemma-dualizing, second proof paragraph, using more-algebra.tex Tag 0A69, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism-technical; Tag 0A67, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate, for the canonical map; Tag 066E, lemma-Noetherian-pseudo-coherent, for the truncation hypothesis. The displayed specialization does not need finite cohomology of L.

proof.text: Step 3 defines $\mathbb D:D_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)^{\mathrm{op}}\to D_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$. Step 4 gives $\operatorname{Id}\cong\mathbb D\mathbb D$ naturally. This isomorphism and its opposite identify both composites of $\mathbb D$ and its opposite with the identity, making them quasi-inverse.

source.place: Tag 0A7C, lemma-dualizing, last sentence of proof.

proof.text: Choose $a\leq b$ supporting the bounded injective representative $J$ of $\Omega$ from Step 2. By [lem-trf-bounded-injective-rhom-amplitude], $K\in D^{\leq c}$ implies $\mathbb D(K)\in D^{\geq a-c}$, and $K\in D^{\geq c}$ implies $\mathbb D(K)\in D^{\leq b-c}$.

source.place: Tag 0A5S, definition-injective-dimension, bounded injective representatives, and dualizing.tex Tag 0A7C, lemma-dualizing, the boundedness clauses; explicit Hom-complex degree calculation after good truncation (old item Step 7).

proof.text: Step 6 gives the forward boundedness implications. For the converses, if $\mathbb D(K)\in D^{\leq d}$ then $K\cong\mathbb D\mathbb D(K)\in D^{\geq a-d}$; if $\mathbb D(K)\in D^{\geq d}$ then $K\in D^{\leq b-d}$. Thus $\mathbb D$ exchanges $D^+_{\mathrm{fg}}$ and $D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}$ and preserves $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}$. The quasi-inverse data of Step 5 restrict to these subcategories.

source.place: Tag 0A7C, lemma-dualizing, restrictions of the anti-equivalence.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BFR, lemma-ubiquity-dualizing, case (2), and Tag 0A7C, lemma-dualizing; elementary canonical-map and degree-bound details written out.
